title: Rate limiting
hook: A gate that allows N requests per window — then starts saying no.

steps.caption: Under the limit, requests pass through to the API.

nodeCaptions.gate: Counters per IP, user, or API key — policy choice.

steps.caption: Too many too fast: the gate blocks. The API never sees the flood.

nodeCaptions.gate: Protects capacity and blunt abuse. Clients should back off.

takeaways: Rate limits cap how often a client may call you.
Blocking at the edge protects backends from stampedes.
Good APIs return clear “try later” signals (e.g. 429).

quiz.question: What is rate limiting mainly for?
choices: Stopping one client from overwhelming a service
